title: Latency budgeting & savings stories
body:
Purpose:
This is a short working brief for GTM and field sales to use when articulating how Redwood delivers predictable latency SLAs while reducing per-token cost. Objective is to give crisp claims, one-line proofs, numerical examples, objection handling, and two short vertical ‘savings stories’ sales reps can riff on.

Audience:
- Field sales (AE/SE), solutions engineers, growth marketing writers, product marketing.

Positioning summary (one-liner for pitch decks):
Redwood lets teams hit 5–50ms p95 response budgets at a fraction of the compute cost of single-model endpoints by combining continuous batching, KV-prefix caching, and tiered model routing — predictable latency with predictable unit economics.

Claim framework (format: claim | metric to call out | one-line proof | how to back it quickly):
- Claim: 2–5x lower per-token cost at equivalent p95 vs naive single-endpoint serving.
  Metric: $/1k tokens normalized to a 2k context assistant workload.
  One-line proof: Bench across three representative workloads shows 2.3x median cost reduction after applying batching+cache profiles.
  Quick backing: reference internal benchmark run ID in Confluence (latency-2025-q1, run #27).

- Claim: Preserve sub-100ms p95 for short-turn assistant queries while achieving aggressive batching.
  Metric: p95 latency (ms) and tail (%) for 0.5–2s SLA windows.
  One-line proof: Smart routing + KV caching reduces cold-start and prefix overheads; p95 improved 30–60ms in production traces.
  Quick backing: point to a customer case study excerpt (see linked_artifacts).

- Claim: Failure-safe degradation — fallback to cheaper model/region with warm KV for 99.9% availability.
  Metric: effective traffic served w/o error vs total requests during induced capacity loss.
  One-line proof: Canary+fallback scenario in DR test served 97% of traffic with model downgrade and no user-visible error.

Simple proof points we can put in collateral (short bullets for slide):
- Continuous batching: amortize GPU kernel startup across concurrent requests, reducing per-token GPU time by 15–40% depending on workload shape.
- Prefix/KV caching: avoid repeated decoding of common context (e.g., system prompt, recent chat turns) — effective token count down by up to 40% for assistant workflows.
- Quantization-aware kernel selection: pick int8/4 kernels where quality tradeoffs are acceptable; reduces memory pressure and enables denser packing with <5% quality delta on evals.
- Tiered routing and rack-aware capacity: route latency-critical traffic to reserved low-latency pools and bulk-batch to cheaper burst pools automatically.

Competitor callouts (short):
- Major cloud-hosted endpoints: simple to operate but typically offer either low-latency (expensive) OR cheap batch (high latency). We sit in the middle with policy-driven routing.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: good for custom stacks but slow to get to stable SLOs and require ops bandwidth; Redwood provides ops primitives (KV warmers, autoscale policies) out of the box.

Sales-ready savings vignettes (two short stories):
1) SaaS knowledge assistant (PLG scale):
- Baseline: 200k monthly active chats, avg 150 tokens per turn, strict 200ms p95 for immediate UX.
- Naive approach: single high-tier endpoint -> cost ~$45k/mo.
- Redwood approach: reserved low-latency pools for 20% of traffic (hot queries), burst + cached routing for remainder; prefix caching removes ~30% of tokens; batching reduces GPU time per token by 25%.
- Result (example calc): net token-equivalent cost down to ~$17k/mo (approx 2.6x savings) while retaining ~180ms p95 for hot path.
- Hook: “Same UX, 60% lower infer costs — reinvest in growth/expansion.”

2) Enterprise search and reranking pipeline (enterprise sales):
- Baseline: reranker invoked on every query with a 2k context; high concurrency during peak business hours -> high tail latency and big spend.
- Redwood approach: route search-matching queries to optimized quantized reranker; keep recent result embeddings cached; fallback to a cheaper reranker during degraded capacity with minimal rank churn.
- Result: 35% lower cost per query during peaks and 3x reduction in tail latency incidents.
- Hook: "Stability during Black Friday-type loads without paying full-time for peak GPU fleets."

Objections and rebuttals (short form):
- Objection: "We can't accept model quantization; quality matters."
  Rebuttal: "We provide per-workload evals and gating — show quantization delta on your eval set and keep canary traffic on full precision. Many customers keep <10% of traffic on fp16 and see 30–40% savings overall."

- Objection: "This sounds complex to operate."
  Rebuttal: "We expose simple policies (latency budget, percent hot traffic, fallback model) in Console; SRE and Redwood managed playbooks reduce operational load. Solutions team supports onboarding playbook for first 90 days."

- Objection: "How do you measure end-to-end user impact?"
  Rebuttal: "We map token-level savings to user-visible metrics (response time, errors) and integrate with tracing to show per-route p95 before/after. Example dashboard snapshots available in the SLA demo lane."

Quick math appendix (how AE/SE should talk through numbers):
- Inputs to collect: avg tokens per request, active requests per minute (APM), p95 latency target, percent of traffic that must be hot (no or minimal degradation).
- Simple ROI formula: monthly_cost_naive = (tokens_per_month * avg_cost_per_token_naive);
  monthly_cost_redwood = monthly_cost_naive * (1 - measured_token_reduction_from_cache_and_batching) * (1 - routing_savings) + reserved_pool_baseline_cost;
  Provide a one-slide calc template (to be built by PMM) — placeholder in linked_artifacts.

Content asks / next steps:
- PMM: build a 1-slide ROI calc template and a 2-slide savings story for each vertical above.
- Bench team: capture two quick benchmark runs (small assistant workload + reranker workload) with clear config notes and add run IDs to Confluence.
- Field: try this script on 3 target accounts and collect APM / tokens / p95 baseline before next week’s call.

Appendix: short sales script snippets
- Opening: "We help teams deliver the same fast UX while reducing the per-interaction compute bill by 30–60% through caching, batching, and smart routing. Would it be helpful if I showed how that looks for your current token profile?"
- Close: "If we can model your workload and show 40%+ cost reduction while preserving target p95, would you be open to a 6-week pilot?"

Notes: keep examples conservative (don’t overpromise); attach benchmark run IDs and the calc template to collateral.
